text:
A very unfinished game.
(A new update has been announced, so take the following with a grain of salt.  I intend to update after I've experienced the update.)

While the game looks nice, and offers a variety of experience, I can't overlook a number of glaring issues with the game-play, mechanics, and design of the game.  It's hard to recommend this game, but to be fair, it's good enough considering the developers aren't some huge studio.  In other-words, I'm giving it a pass.

The Pros.
Space looks beautiful, the sound design is a 9.5 out of 10.  The variety of environments and items are a 7 out of 10.  The puzzles are the best part of this game, and are genuinely satisfying to solve.  Just exploring, and finding little secrets in this detailed environment while getting immersed in the sounds and music is a worth while experience.  Being able to personalize your ship is nice, but feels very limited without the extra DLC, which really should be just a basic part of the game.


The Cons
The game is buggy, broken, and under-developed.  For a game so focused on immersion, and even a touch of simulation, instilling that feeling of actually drifting through space, there are some decisions that break that immersion.  Why does the headlight barely light up anything in front of you?  You're more likely to crash in caves than actually make out where you're going with the light.  Why does the inertia dampener add extra thrust to the ship, as opposed to being an auto stabilization system?  Why do you move slower with the dampeners off, when realistically, you should be able to move with more responsiveness with the system giving you full control.  I love the feeling of floating in Zero-G, but it makes no sense that the dampeners make the thrust of the ship stronger.  Also, why is there no compass?  All the settings there are for the UI, and you couldn't give a simple compass graphic to help the player keep oriented?  This isn't even a crazy, unrealistic idea, ships have compasses.  Even in the cockpit, how is there no compass?  Also, of all the games that have been made with air, or space combat, and sci-fi themes, how is there no radar?  Why is there not an actual graphical display to let you see your surroundings?  It's not about realism, it's about presenting information to the player that the player actually needs.  Also, also, and critically, how is there no cloud navigation?  This one was a minor grievance, but after getting the DLC smokescreen, and seeing that the UI actually outlines structures so you can navigate through the fog, HOW IS THIS NOT JUST A STANDARD FEATURE!?  The anxiety I get in cloudy areas make me want to vomit, and to think that there actually is a function in the game to fix this, but they just restricted it feels like they just intentionally wanted to leave the game inaccessible to people who suffer with these phobias and anxiety.  Hell, this could have been a special radar for all I care.

The Cons pt 2
After reaching the end of the game, maxing my level, and starting to build my ship into a boss, and switching to nightmare mode, I started to notice a few things.  The combat experiences suck.  The strategy starts to disappear, and it becomes more of a pick your favorite toy, and fire till all the red markers disappear.  Again, this is Nightmare Mode.  The enemies don't feel engaging, or intelligent really.  The difficulty just revolves around boosted enemy health and damage.  Energy damage vs Kinetic damage hardly seems to matter, as there's not enough of a difference for it to really require thinking about.  The enemies themselves are all just moving things to shoot, some having more health, or speed than others.  The teleporters are annoying, not in a bad way, and the frontal shield enemies are slightly annoying.  The most engaging enemy I can think of is honestly the bomb thrower, a stationary base turret that literally just lobs bombs at you.  The turret has a massive shield that constantly recharges, and the bombs disable shields, so what you're meant to do is catch the bomb, and through it back to bring down it's shield, and then empty it's small health pool.  Now, I know this, but I'm stubborn. and I like to prove my dominance, so I ignored the bombs, and just blasted it with autocannon or beam laser fire to drain the shield without it having a chance to recharge.  This is the only enemy that I feel actually gives options of how to deal with it.  The third option being corrosion missiles, as they ignore the shield entirely for the easiest kill.  This is the only enemy in the game I can talk about, because all the others are just boring damage sponges, big or small.  The Okkar shield drone being the only other exception, as auto aim reflects off the shield, but if you carefully aim at the frame near the edge, you can do direct damage.  The combat is boring, and some of the best weapons are either limited, or under-whelming.  The cruise missile acts like a nuke, but explodes like a firecracker, while the Bomber Ultimate is this massive static ball of "destruction" that barely does damage.  All this being said, I don't know why you can't customize weapon energy color.

The Glitches
So, the game not only suffers from bad design issues, but also buggy, lazy code that either needed more polish, or just to be properly developed in the first place.  At this point, I understand that the game has been out for a while, and supposedly isn't even getting updates anymore.  That being said, how are some of these glitches still a thing, and weren't fixed within months after release?  The Inventory system is one of the buggiest I've seen in any game, ever.  Catalyst affects will get stuck, and apply to an item that doesn't have it, item perks will randomly break, such as Reinforced hull not giving you the +100% hull, or Hazard Armor just not applying the immunity while you actively have armor.  I have in multiple occasions had to shuffle my modules to force the game to reset my stats, sometimes more than once in the same area.  How did this even get through play testing?  Do the devs at all care about the actual game-play, and stability of the experience?  I literally feel like I can't even trust the stats, or perks to do what they say, cause sometimes the game just doesn't feel like applying the rules.  Invisibility at times doesn't work, no shooting, or boosting, I just get shot anyway.

I feel I've said enough, not even personal opinion, but just focusing on objective, structural facts.  The game is broken, and under-developed.  There are basic mechanics, that not only should be implemented, but features that seem to be thrown together with duct tape and gum, as if they didn't care if it worked.  I feel this is saying enough, without even getting into my personal opinions about what I would have liked.  It bothers me deeply that this game has so much potential, but is plagued so deeply by bad design choices, or lazy feature implementation.

But space is still pretty, flying is good enough, and the puzzles are nice, so is it worth it?  In my opinion, it's not as good as it could be, but there's still a solid experience to be had, even if a lot is missing, or falling apart.  It's a nice beta of an incomplete game.

text:
[h2] Gameplay [/h2]
RimWorld is a 2D sandbox colony-building and survival game. Your main goal is to keep the inhabitants of your colony "pawns" alive, strengthen your settlement, and ultimately build a spaceship to escape the planet, if you like. The world map also features various friendly, hostile, and neutral factions that you can establish different relationships with. But the focus of the game lies in the various events you experience, the combat, the construction of your colony and production within the base. The game is exceptionally detailed, even though I only played the base game, it kept me hooked for a long time. The DLCs are said to “enhance” the experience to completely different levels, so they are highly recommended. And I must say that the game has a massive modding community with an endless amount of content, which you should really try out. 
[h2] Graphics [/h2]
The game has 2D graphics with a unique style. If graphics are very important for you, you may not like this game. It has a top-down and tile-based (squares) look. Personally, I use mods to make the game textures look better, and it looks much nicer this way.
[h2] Audio [/h2]
The audio in the game is classic one. There is nothing special or great to praise here. The music and sound effects are simple, but they are enough for this kind of game. It does not bother you while playing, but do not expect anything amazing. I muted the music when I was playing.
[h2] Story [/h2]
Without DLCs (I didn’t play them), the story is about a group of people stranded on a planet. They meet new people, build a colony, and try to escape the planet with a spaceship at the end. However, RimWorld is a sandbox game, so you can choose other endings too. For example, you can stay on the planet forever or destroy other factions. You can change the story settings at the start of the game, and you can also use mods to make it different. 
[h2] Difficulty [/h2]
The game has different difficulty levels depending on your scenario, the storytellers (they control the events in the game), where you live, and the factions around you. Of course, you can choose a difficulty level at the start of the game. You should especially check the storytellers. There are many difficulty options, from very easy to hardcore mode.

text:
I'd played this game through twice on the Xbox before buying it on here, and now I'm playing it through a 3rd time. I love this game. If you're into Stardew Valley you'll either love or hate this game because it's so extremely similar while also feeling very different. The gameplay is almost identical, but I enjoy the characters in this far, far more. They feel more fleshed out, more human, more interesting, and just generally more engaging.
I find the graphics far more enjoyable in this than in Stardew (which obviously is just a matter of preference, so your mileage WILL vary), though I will admit that it's only now, playing it on the PC that I get to actually see those graphics in decent detail. My SAD Xbox runs the graphics incredibly poorly. But when you can see the detail they've added to scenery, it's genuinely heartwarming. The kids have little paper plate face decorations in the classroom! It's adorable!
I find the farming fairly enjoyable (honestly, it's never my favourite part of any farming game) and the ranching is fairly fun, with the animals being genuinely cute, and with luwaks, peacocks, quails, ostriches, buffalo, and alpacas, not to mention the underwater creatures you can farm, it's a good expansion on the usual farm animals that have gotten a bit samey over the years of cozy farm games.
Clearing the ocean and becoming a merfolk is easily my favourite feature in the game. Some people find the garbage-clearing a bit tedious, but I find it incredibly meditative to just vibe in the currents, swinging a scythe, and seeing it all get cleaner. It's genuinely peaceful. 
But it's the characters that make Coral Island. I love them. They're so detailed, so fun, so varied. I love almost all of them, and love to hate the rest. Getting to know them over the months and years is so fun and so heartwarming, and it's exactly what brings me back time and time again. It's what kept me playing on the xbox back when it first released despite a bug that caused it to crash at the start of EVERY SINGLE DAY forcing me to restart my xbox every single in-game night. No other game has kept me playing through that kind of frustration. It doesn't crash like that anymore, by the way, just in case anyone was worried.

TLDR: If you like cozy farming, cozy animals, merfolk, and lovable NPCs, and you DON'T think Stardew Valley is the absolute pinnacle of cozy gaming, you'll enjoy this.

text:
I want to start off by saying that I didn't (and still don't to a certain extent) really like 2D games or isometric games because of the obvious limitations that come with them and the usual jank that comes from developers trying to work with them, so buying Rimworld was sort of a choice that I thought I'd end up regretting later. Rimworld managed to make up to this and deliver MUCH more with the amount of depth and content it offers, even without any DLCs or mods. By this alone it has kind of mediated me into playing more 2D games and that should already give you an idea of how incredible this game is.

The game is quite intuitive aside from a couple game mechanics, the player is also supported by the tutorial and the in game learning helper that gives tips and information based on whatever you're doing. The only guide I watched on this game was of a mod called combat extended (more on that later). The aforementioned mechanics such as wealth have somewhat of a niche to them and may need further dwelling to get a grasp of but is absolutely not required for casual gameplay and usually people only learn them to get an advantage in harder challenges. It's also very polished, I can't remember the last time I had an actual bug with one of the base game components.

Because of the game's sandbox nature, you can pretty much do whatever you want to with your game and colony. It's important to mention that despite this, the game gives you a narrative and an actual objective (This is completely up to you if you want to actually finish it or not) with progression, which is very welcome in the day and age where games use sandbox as a cope to not actually give their game meaningful progression. It also goes very hand in hand with the emergent goals you give your colony during your playthrough and doesn't get in the way. 

Your pawns, or colonists, are not hard to manage and are quite cooperative all things considered. It also doesn't give off the feeling that you are controlling dumb robot while doing so, with factors such as their mood and personality traits being considered whenever they do an action. Occasionally the pawns might do stupid ♥♥♥♥ like path into a insect hive because they wanted to haul a corpse, but things like this are also avoidable with area management. Of course with the game being a colony simulator, you'll have to take care of their mood, social... and make sure your colonist with a chemical fascination doesn't have access to your cocaine stash for example.

The vanilla combat (especially the ranged combat) is somewhat mediocre and quite RNG based, but can be played around in your favor with some tactics. I normally abhor the idea of judging a game based on it's extensions and mods for reasons but Combat Extended is such an incredibly good mod that takes the only weak point (hence why I had to mention it) of the game in my opinion and turns it into one of the strongest. Seriously, the only reason I believe something of this order isn't implemented in the base game is because it changes a bit too much especially with other mods in the mix. 

Another major selling point of the game is that it's more of a storyteller than a traditional strategy game. This is mostly apparent and is quite well integrated into the game with features such as dialogs and social relations between characters. But in my opinion the usual gameplay consists more of emergent tales and events than a whole, smooth story. This isn't to say you can't get actual stories but the gameplay does favor small but numerous ones.

There is a lot more to say about Rimworld that I couldn't dream of squeezing into this review because of it's plethora of features and even more that the DLCs add. As for the DLCs, I think most are also well made but it's up to debate if they are worth their prices or not. Overall I found Rimworld to be a great game and it's downsides quickly overshadowed by it's very fun and easily remediable gameplay.

text:
I really like this game! I like the art, I ADORE the pets. Allowing me to have rabbits, foxes, or my personal fav; a bearded dragon is way awesome, There are some minor errors that make playing an annoyance sometimes though. Example; when you switch items while moving, it makes you either stop completely, makes it so you can no longer turn until you stop and start again, or places an invisible wall in front of you so you can't continue until you stop and start moving again. It's also impossible to reorganize your inventory when you're in a chest view, because it will automatically go into the chest instead of letting you pick it up. I would really like to not feel the need to exit the chest view, to go to my inventory view, and then reorganize before going back into the chest because I inevitably forgot to put something away due to my inventory being disorganized. Just a bit frustrating, In cutscenes, clicking onto the next stage of text keeps popping up a "skip cutscene" notification at the top of the screen, which is soo incredibly distracting and makes it hard to not be pulled out of the scenes. Additionally, I really wish that if you find a note with peoples likes and things it could add them to their list, because it is hard and annoying to go through the notes to find if maybe at one point it was possibly mentioned that someone liked something. It's also fairly hard to get people to like you, and I was unfortunate enough that the required gift to make and give for the tutorial quests were items disliked or hated by the two people I was most interested in getting to know, so they started off in the worst way possible for me. I do really like the characters, I like how many people there are to get to know, and it really feels like there is someone to romance for everyone (Although with all of the guests who visit in I know they could do an awesome goth romanceable, and I wish for that more than anything I've ever wished before due to that. I know they can do it really well, but they chose not to for whatever reason.) I do also wish I could turn off Sunny shouting constantly, I can't stand him because reading his dialogue makes me uncomfortable and upset. It feels overwhelming, and so I avoid him at all costs, and try to skip through cutscenes with him. All in all, this game is really fun, and I enjoy a lot of things about it, but there are some tweaks needed to make it better. I know I spent a lot of time talking about issues I've experienced, but I really do like and recommend this game. At the moment, I've played 33 hours and I am only now getting people to 2 hearts, and scratching the surface of the story. I am now on my first day of fall, so it seems as though this will all be a slow burn for sure, It is a great time sink, especially if you really like simulation games. I'd equate it more to a rune factory or harvest moon type than a stardew or fields of mistria type, so keep that in mind when purchasing!

EDIT: So, immediately after posting this review I hopped on to play, and my steam notified me that I lost 3 weeks of in-game play. This lost my farm's automations, a handful of fast travel waypoints, a town rank, tons of hearts from people, my museum upgrade, a bunch of donations to my alters and museum, a good number of mine levels, and tons of levels in general in diving, mining, and other things, This was really disappointing, and honestly made me not want to even replay. I saw from a reviewer previously that he had lost 3 game saves entirely, and this has me nervous and honestly upset. This is the reason I held off soo long before purchasing this game, and now I'm dreading playing it instead of enjoying the game. Hope this doesn't happen again, because it may just not be worth playing in that case.

text:
Controversial take incoming but I think at its core, Payday 3 is better than 2. It’s got the better gunplay, movement and the interactions of each heist feel less tedious than they do in 2. But obviously this game lacks a in a lot of areas meaning that no it’s not better than 2 as of right now as a whole. Less heists, less build variety, less things worth grinding for like Infamy in 2. But I feel bad comparing this to its predecessor that’s had 10+ years of content put into it so I’m gonna review it more as its own thing.

Payday 3 is incredibly fun, either solo or with friends. The gunplay feels fluid and snappy, while I haven’t delved into every single heist yet, from what I have played none of them are bad and I’ve enjoyed figuring out how to go loud or stealthy in each one I can. The devs are constantly working at reworking heists that may not have met expectations and they really have taken community feedback into account with improving the game. I didn’t play at launch so I’m sure there are a lot of players burned but I think the game has come a long way since that point and I want to support it so it continues improving and gives us the game we deserve. As a studying game developer, I like watching comeback stories like these where devs get the chance to learn from their mistakes. I think if you’re mildly curious, pick the game up on sale.

text:
For once I cannot think of any quips or play on words for the opening to this review other than the predictable, thus - I shall skip.
-------------------
[b] Swinging into the positives [/b]
[b] Graphics; [/b] They are utterly beautiful, notably the characters and the costume designs. For some reason it's extremely appealing to look at all the stitching and details within the suits - it's also the first game where it's made me happy to take screenshots, and may do it more for other games because wow it was extremely satisfying.

[b] Story; [/b] Ending made me cry but also made me want to hop straight into the next game

[b] The World [/b] It's great. Very fun to just swing around like a clown and then fly into an enemy at 500mph and the picture opportunity is endless - pure beauty. There is of plenty to do to keep you on the toes but I feel like that's done to hide the short plot but I'll go into that more in the Negative part. 

[b] Combat [/b] Pure joy. Love any game combat that is very free flow, Batman, Sleeping Dogs. Just perfect and it's quite fun to mesh up combos with ariel shots and grapples and gadgets. Speaking of love all the gadgets, really didn't think I'd use all of them but they all had their strengths with no real weaknesses

[b] Negatives [/b] 
[b] Story; [/b] I know I put positive but at the same time the story felt way too short and I was quite disappointed at the lack of reaction at the reveal of the demon leader and they cheaply did a time skip. Also the missions as MJ and Miles we're just not it for me. I get it for building his story and making her useful but it's never fun. Though it made me realise how bad the enemy AI as you can easily sneak past [Then again for NG+ achievement, a short story is bliss but the bigger picture etc]

[b] The World; [/b] Again I said I'd cover the negative here - I love the facts there's loads to do, the variety is great but some of it is an absolute drag, the research stations felt somewhat slow and just wasn't interested. Some of the Taskmaster challenges such as the drone chasing and Screwball.. hated them. A big one as well is the wave of enemy bases. While it's fun to beat 'em up for 6 waves, it should've been that if you don't alert them for the whole first round then it finishes early. Especially when in the Sable DLC. 

Overall it's a great game and fun to achievement hunt, but like most games I plan to finish this year, NG+ runs feel like a complete chore, I tend to take a break after doing it first time round as I did with this game a couple years ago, and after realising how long the campaign is, it made it easier but doesn't take away from how jarring it is as an achievement.

8.7/10 rating
